transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. What brings you in to see me?

Well, I guess I'm here because of work. I'm in HR, and... well, I'm on leave right now. It's a whole thing. See, I pushed ahead with this massive onboarding launch. I mean, we really needed it, the old system was just archaic, like something out of the 90s, you know? I remember my first day there, they handed me this literal binder—a binder!—and I thought, 'I have a master's degree, why am I looking at tabbed dividers?' Anyway, I committed company money and vendor time to the new launch before the actual approvals were in place. At the time, it felt so bold and necessary, like I was finally cutting through the red tape. I was reading this book on disruptive leadership, actually, and it really resonated with me. But... yeah, now I'm on leave, and everyone is asking what I was thinking. My boss was so furious, she had this vein popping out on her forehead, which I've never seen before. She usually drinks that calming chamomile tea all day. But yeah, that's why I'm here.
Around the time you launched this project, did you notice you needed much less sleep than usual, or that your mood felt unusually elevated, energetic, or irritable compared to how you normally feel?

Yeah, exactly that. For the past few weeks, I've felt just... brilliantly alive. Like I could finally show leadership what HR can actually be, you know? Not just paper pushers, but real strategic partners. But on the flip side, I'd get suddenly furious if someone questioned me. Like, even over tiny things—small edits to my presentation or routine budget questions. I'd just snap. 

Speaking of budget questions, it was Greg in Finance who really started nitpicking the vendor costs. He's always been so difficult, ever since the 2019 company holiday party. We had this massive argument because he wanted to hire a taco truck, and I was like, "Greg, it's a winter gala, people are wearing velvet and silk. You can't have them dripping salsa everywhere." I mean, have you seen the price of dry cleaning lately? I took my wool overcoat in on Tuesday and the guy charged me forty-five dollars. Just to clean a coat! I almost walked out. It’s absolute highway robbery, the way they upcharge for wool. I should probably just start buying polyester, but it doesn't breathe at all. 

But... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, my mood. Yeah, definitely. Brilliantly alive or just furious, not much in between.

Before these past few weeks, have you ever had a period—lasting days or longer—where you felt unusually low, hopeless, or lost interest in things, or a separate earlier time when you felt this same kind of high energy and mood?

Low or hopeless? I mean... I don't think so? Not really. I've always been a pretty driven guy. Though, I guess I was incredibly bored when I worked at this logistics firm back in 2015. But that wasn't like, a medical hopelessness, it was just the environment. They had zero natural light in the HR department. None. Just these awful, buzzing fluorescent tubes overhead. 

It’s actually terrible for employee morale, I don't know if you know that. I read this massive study on workplace ergonomics and natural light. They did it in Denmark, I think? Or maybe Sweden. Somewhere with dark winters. Anyway, they brought in all these sunlight simulators and productivity went up by something crazy, like 40 percent. I actually tried to pitch that to my boss at the time, but he was this incredibly rigid guy who thought even having a potted plant on your desk was a security risk. A security risk! Like someone's gonna hide corporate secrets in a ficus. 

People are so paranoid. My neighbor is exactly like that, actually. He just installed six different security cameras pointing at his driveway because a kid rode a bike over his grass once. And the grass isn't even nice! It's mostly crabgrass and dandelions. I spend every single weekend out there pulling weeds, aerating the soil, putting down fertilizer, and he just lets his lawn go completely to seed. It all blows over into my yard. It's infuriating. Have you ever tried to get rid of crabgrass once it takes root? You basically have to dig up the whole yard. 

But, uh... wait. What were we talking about? Oh, right, feeling low or having this high energy before. No, I don't think I've ever felt like this before. It's really just been these last few weeks.

During these past few weeks of feeling this way, have you experienced anything like hearing voices or sounds others couldn't hear, or holding beliefs—like having special powers, a special mission, or being targeted by others—that friends or family found unusual or untrue?

Voices? Special powers? No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I'm just an HR guy, I'm not a superhero. Though honestly, with the amount of conflict resolution I have to do on a daily basis, sometimes I feel like I need superpowers just to get through a Tuesday. 

Like last week, before I got put on leave, I had to mediate this dispute between two developers who were literally shouting at each other over the air conditioning. One wanted it at 68 degrees, the other wanted it at 72. 68 is freezing, by the way. You can't type if your fingers are numb! I read this article on thermal comfort in open-plan offices, and it turns out women actually prefer warmer temperatures because their metabolic rates are different. It's fascinating stuff, really. It made me want to completely overhaul our facilities management policies. I even started drafting a proposal for individualized micro-climate zones at every desk. You'd need these specialized HVAC vents, of course, which are expensive, but think of the productivity gains! 

But the facilities manager, Dave, he's so old school. He still uses a flip phone. A flip phone! In this day and age. How do you even check your email on that? I tried to show him how to use the new company app, and he just stared at me like I was speaking Greek. It's so frustrating trying to innovate when you're surrounded by people who are stuck in 2005. I swear, if I have to explain cloud storage to one more person...

Anyway, what was the question? Oh, voices and stuff. No, no, I haven't heard or seen anything that isn't there. Just... you know, trying to fix the very real problems right in front of me.
